record.paper_title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
record.original_question: What analysis tools can interrogate self-modifying, evolving, open-ended systems once they move outside their current behavioral models and outside measures based on those models?

evidence.quote:
What are appropriate analysis tools for interrogating self-modifying, evolving,
open systems?
An open ended system will eventually move outside its current model of behavior, and hence outside any
measure based on that model [110]. This makes designing analysis tools challenging.

Analysis tools exist, for example, the MODES (‘Measurements of Open-
ended Dynamics in Evolving Systems’) toolbox [121], which has been applied to a range of self-modifying
systems, including ecologies and major evolutionary transitions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a dynamical system S that is self-modifying and open-ended in the following informal sense: at any time t, the behavior of S is described by some model M_t drawn from a (possibly unbounded) family of admissible models, together with an associated set of observables and measures μ_{M_t}. The system is called open-ended if, for every t and every choice of model M_t, there exists a future time t' > t at which the realized behavior of S lies outside the descriptive scope of M_t and cannot be quantified by any measure in μ_{M_t}.

Develop a formal framework of analysis tools (i.e., a class of model-independent observables, invariants, or detection procedures) capable of interrogating such self-modifying, evolving, open-ended systems even after their behavior has escaped any fixed model M_t and any measure based on M_t. Specifically:

(a) Give a rigorous definition of an "analysis tool" T that is well-defined on trajectories of S without requiring a fixed background model.

(b) Identify necessary and sufficient conditions under which such a tool T can detect, quantify, or classify novel behavior of S that lies outside the current model M_t.

(c) Construct at least one explicit example of such a tool, and prove that it remains informative across model transitions M_t → M_{t'}.

(d) Determine whether a universal analysis tool — one that remains informative for every open-ended system in a specified class — can exist, or prove an impossibility result analogous to model-based incompleteness.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conceptual open problem about analysis methodology for open-ended evolving systems. Existing tools such as the MODES toolbox provide partial measures of open-ended dynamics, but no universal model-independent framework is known. The problem appears to remain open in the artificial life and complex systems literature.

status_evidence.title: MODES toolbox for open-ended evolution
status_evidence.snippet: The MODES toolbox provides metrics (change, novelty, complexity, ecology) for measuring open-ended evolutionary dynamics, but is acknowledged to be a partial, not universal, set of measures.
status_evidence.claim: Existing tools provide partial measurement of open-ended dynamics; a general framework remains open.

status_evidence.title: Open-Ended Evolution: Perspectives from the OEE Workshop
status_evidence.snippet: The community identifies the lack of model-independent analysis tools as a central open challenge for studying open-ended systems.
status_evidence.claim: The need for analysis tools that work outside fixed behavioral models is recognized as an open problem.
